lessonDescription: Use this when the teacher gives an idea or premise for a story: you write the story yourself in Yarn, following the fiction authoring guide, which gives a better story than the generated story templates. The teacher does not need to have a script. You choose the story type, and supply the complete story with picture placeholders, one image prompt per placeholder, an image prompt for the poster, and an image style. The story is used exactly as you wrote it. The template generates the pictures and the poster, and builds 2 items: a content page with the poster, and a fiction item with a picture for every placeholder.

user_topic.title: Story Summary
user_topic.description: Optional. A one or two sentence summary of the story. It is saved as the lesson's topic.

user_text.title: Fiction Story
user_text.description:
An interactive fiction story written in Yarn format. Do not write it from memory: first call mod_minilesson_aigen_fetch_item_type_details with itemtype "fiction" and follow the authoringguide it returns, which covers the yarn syntax this player supports and how to structure a story worth reading.

Place the picture commands as the authoring guide directs: at the top of the node, as the first line after the '---' divider. The filenames are two digits counting up from 01.png with no gaps, to a maximum of 30 (01.png, 02.png ... 09.png, 10.png).

user_customdata1.title: Image Style
user_customdata1.description: The image style for all the pictures: the poster and every story picture. It is used for each image prompt that does not name a style of its own.

user_customdata2.title: Image Prompts

user_customdata3.title: Poster Image Prompt
user_customdata3.description: An image generation prompt for the square poster image on the story's intro page. Describe the main characters in one scene that represents the story. The poster is made from this prompt only, so describe the characters' looks and the setting here too. The Image Style is used unless the prompt names a style of its own. Do not ask for text in the image.

user_customdata4.title: Story Type
user_customdata4.description: The shape of the story you write. "Story with choices" is narrative fiction (Part 3A of the fiction authoring guide): a plot moves on and the learner's choices change what happens. "Explore a place" is spatial fiction (Part 3B): the learner moves between places, finds things and uses them. The template does not read this value, it tells you which kind of story to write. If the user has not said which they want, ask them before you write the story, because changing it later means writing the story again.
